title: Your Child's Real World: Discovery Through the Five Senses and Free Play
summary:
Imagine your little one, holding a wooden spoon and tapping it on a metal pot, or burying their tiny hands in a plate of mashed pasta, or staring at a dewdrop on a leaf. These simple moments are their real world, where all their senses interact with their surroundings. A screen, despite its attractive colors and varied sounds, confines them to only sight and hearing, separating them from the joy of touch, smell, and taste, which are fundamental to their discovery of the world at this early age.

Your child's healthy development in their early years largely depends on this comprehensive sensory exploration. When they play freely, touch different surfaces, listen to the sounds of nature, smell the scent of flowers, and taste food with their tiny fingers, they develop their sensory experiences and learn how to interact with the world around them in a real and effective way—skills supported by free play and direct interaction more than by screens.

Our role as parents is not to be trainers, but to be providers of a safe and inspiring environment. You can give them an empty box, a collection of fabrics with different textures, or even some leaves and twigs you gathered from the garden. Let your child lead their own discovery, and gently step back to give them space and freedom to create and learn. Trust that these moments of free play are among the most beneficial things you can offer them to grow and thrive.
try_this: Tonight: Prepare a small basket containing 3-4 safe items with different textures (e.g., a wooden spoon, a soft cloth, a bath loofah, a wool ball). Place it next to your child and let them explore it freely for 5 minutes.
